item.title: How not to get stuck with solutions to problems you helped fix
item.description: As a senior developer or technical leader, you are often called in to solve urgent problems. There’s nothing inherently wrong with that—it’s often part of your job description. However, after fixing the immediate issue, there’s a risk that you get drawn into a continuous cycle of improving that area. You’ve resolved a critical problem and are now seen as a key person for that domain, and this pattern repeats as you get pulled into other firefighting activities.
